# omp-advisor-consensus

An adversarial loop between omp's **advisor** and the **main agent**. The
advisor reviews each turn; every finding the agent has not answered becomes a
continuation turn that quotes the finding, demands a fix or an evidence-backed
rebuttal, and re-reviews. The run only settles when the advisor raises nothing
further **and** the agent does not claim its own work is still open.

Think Ralph loop (`while not done: run again`), but with a second model as the
termination oracle, a per-prompt round budget, a repeat detector, and an audit
ledger persisted in the session.

Off by default. Nothing runs until you arm it.

## Install

```bash
# local checkout (symlinked, edits are live)
omp plugin link /home/asdf/Downloads/omp-advisor-consensus

# git
omp plugin install github:alosslessdev/omp-advisor-consensus

# marketplace (this repo ships .omp-plugin/marketplace.json)
omp plugin marketplace add alosslessdev/omp-advisor-consensus
omp plugin install advisor-consensus@omp-advisor-consensus

# one-off
omp --extension /home/asdf/Downloads/omp-advisor-consensus/extensions/consensus.ts
```

Requires the advisor subsystem to be usable: set `advisor.enabled: true` and a
resolvable `advisor` model role (or a `WATCHDOG.yml` roster). The plugin warns
once per session when the advisor is off.

## Turning it on

```text
/adversarial              # toggle: on <-> off (off cancels)
/adversarial on           # arm for this session
/adversarial pause        # stop acting, keep the episode and its round budget
/adversarial resume       # continue the same episode
/adversarial off          # disarm and cancel the in-flight episode
/adversarial status       # mode, advisor, config, sync policy, round, converged count
/adversarial config       # TUI editor for rounds, repeats, severity, notify, sync, model
/adversarial max 12       # rounds for this session (1..100)
/adversarial repeats 4    # re-raises of one finding before escalation (1..10)
/adversarial severity concern
/adversarial require-stop off # allow silence to close (default: required)
/adversarial model session     # default: advisor runs the session's live model
/adversarial model configured  # use modelRoles.advisor / the WATCHDOG entry model
/adversarial sync off     # release the advisor.syncBacklog pin
```

Arming brings the reviewer up: if `advisor.enabled` is false, `/adversarial on`
(or a resumed session that was armed) overrides it to true for this session,
runtime-only, cleared by `/adversarial off` and on shutdown. Nothing is written
to your config. If the override is unavailable the plugin says so with a
transient toast instead of looking broken later.

Arming is recorded in the session transcript, so `/adversarial on` survives
`omp --resume`. The plugin also re-reads `advisor.enabled` at every settle, so
`/advisor on` mid-session is picked up without a restart.

`/adversarial config` opens a TUI editor for the live values; the same numbers
can be passed inline (`max`, `repeats`, `severity`) or set durably through
plugin settings:

```bash
omp plugin config --set enabled=true            # ~/.omp/plugins/omp-plugins.lock.json
omp plugin config --set maxRounds=12
omp plugin config --set maxRepeats=4
omp plugin config --set minSeverity=concern
```

While the loop is armed, the status line next to the message box keeps showing
the effective configuration and the live round:

```text
adversarial on · 100 rounds · repeats 3
adversarial 4/100 · 2 open
adversarial paused · 4/100
adversarial converged · 4/100
```

`off` is not `pause`: off writes a `settled: "cancelled"` marker for the active
episode, so a late advisor card cannot restart it. Pause leaves the ledger
untouched; resume continues from the same round.

## Loop

```text
user prompt
    |
    v
agent turn  --->  advisor review (forced synchronous while armed)
    |                    |
    |            findings after the last assistant message?
    |                    |
    |             no ----+---- yes
    |             |             |
    |             v             v
    |        settle       continuation turn with the ledger
    |                          |
    +--------------------------+   (round++ up to maxRounds)
```

Agreement is two-sided:

- **advisor side** — either an explicit stop call, or silence. Silence is why
  the plugin pins `advisor.syncBacklog` to `strict`: without it the final review
  can still be in flight at settle time, and "nothing yet" would be mistaken for
  "nothing to say".
- **agent side** — the reply must not end with `verdict: open`. Agent silence is
  fine; an explicit admission of open work escalates instead of converging.

### Who decides convergence

The advisor. Its `advise(note: "[converged] …")` call is evaluated before the
round budget and overrides even the agent's own `verdict: open`; the plugin only
decides whether to spend another turn. The call itself is not forwarded to the
agent as work — it is recorded in the ledger as `viaStopCall` and stays visible
in the transcript as an advisor card.

That is the default (`requireStopCall: true`): an episode that ends without an
explicit call escalates with the open list instead of being recorded as
agreement. Because the default reviewer prompt asks the advisor to speak only
with evidence, and the host's emission guard drops content-free notes (`stop`,
`done`, `lgtm`), the loop needs the stop-call guidance to know the protocol —
copy [`examples/WATCHDOG.md`](examples/WATCHDOG.md) into your `WATCHDOG.md`.

`/adversarial require-stop off` (or `requireStopCall=false`) brings back
silence-as-agreement: cheaper for a reviewer that only speaks when it has
something to say, at the cost of an implicit decision.

### The advisor's stop call

Advisor tool grants come from the built-in catalog only, so a plugin cannot hand
the advisor a dedicated `stop` tool. The tool it always has is `advise`, so the
stop call is a reserved note:

```text
advise(note: "[converged] every finding is fixed or soundly rebutted")
```

That call closes the episode immediately (even over a `verdict: open` from the
agent) and is never counted as a finding. A note that arrives in the same batch
as a real finding is ignored — nobody stops mid-objection. To teach the advisor
the protocol, copy [`examples/WATCHDOG.md`](examples/WATCHDOG.md) into your
project or user `WATCHDOG.md`. The short version:

```markdown
When nothing is left to raise, call `advise` once with
`[converged] <one-line reason>`. That call ends the adversarial loop; silence
also ends it, but the call is explicit and audited.
```

Every finding enters a ledger keyed by normalized text. A finding the advisor
re-raises `maxRepeats` times escalates to the operator rather than spinning, and
the round budget caps the whole exchange.

### Late notes

…

…
MIT

# omp-advisor-consensus
…
## Loop
…
### Late notes

A review that finishes *after* the run settled cannot wake the agent: the host
preserves it as a card and stays idle. The plugin catches advisor messages for
ten minutes after `agent_end`, and when one lands unanswered it reopens the
converged episode, spends the next round, and steers the agent itself. A
cancelled or escalated episode never reopens.

## What the agent sees

Each continuation carries a machine-shaped block, not a paraphrase:

```xml
<advisor-consensus round="2" max_rounds="4">
The advisor reviewed your last turn and left findings open. ...
Open findings:
1. [concern] advisor="Architecture" Missing regression test for the new parser branch
2. [blocker] Division by zero is unhandled
...
Close your reply with exactly this block:
<convergence>
1: fixed | rebutted | blocked — one line of evidence
2: ...
verdict: closed | open
</convergence>
</advisor-consensus>
```

The agent keeps the right to disagree — advisor notes are advisory — but a
rebuttal needs evidence the advisor has not already rejected.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `false` | Arm the loop. Off until you turn it on. |
| `minSeverity` | `nit` | Lowest finding severity that keeps the loop running. |
| `maxRounds` | `100` | Continuations per user prompt (configurable 1..100). |
| `maxRepeats` | `3` | Re-raises of the same finding before escalation (1..10). |
| `forceSyncBacklog` | `true` | Pin `advisor.syncBacklog: strict` while armed. |
| `useSessionModel` | `true` | Default the advisor to the session's live model. |
| `requireStopCall` | `true` | Strict agreement: only the advisor's `[converged]` call closes; silence escalates. |
| `notify` | `true` | Toast per round, convergence, and escalation. |

Env overrides for one process: `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_ENABLED`,
`OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MIN_SEVERITY`, `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MAX_ROUNDS`,
`OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MAX_REPEATS`, `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_FORCE_SYNC_BACKLOG`,
`OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_USE_SESSION_MODEL`, `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_NOTIFY`.

### Advisor model

An adversarial loop is most informative when both sides are comparable, so the
default advisor model is whatever the session is running: the plugin pins
`modelRoles.advisor` to the live `provider/id` and re-pins it after a `/model`
switch. Two things win over that default:

- an explicitly configured `modelRoles.advisor` (the plugin reads
  `isConfigured` before touching it and leaves your choice alone),
- a `WATCHDOG.yml` roster entry with its own `model` — roster models bypass the
  role entirely.

`/adversarial model configured` restores the role-based resolution for the
session.

## When it stays out of the way

- advisor subsystem disabled
- plan mode active (only user-driven turns resolve plan reviews)
- errored or aborted turns
- sessions that are not the main agent (subagents, task children)
- an episode already settled for the current user prompt
- paused, or turned off

## Limits

- Rounds 1-6 ride the host's `session_stop` continuation (capped at 8 per
  prompt, shared with advisor continuations). Later rounds are steered from
  `agent_end` as agent-initiated turns, which is what lets `maxRounds` reach
  100. Verified headless: rounds 1-6 arrive as `session-stop-continuation`, round
  7 onward as an `advisor-consensus` turn. A process that is already disposing
  can drop the final steered turn.
- A 100-round budget is a ceiling, not a target: each round is one agent turn
  plus one advisor review. `maxRepeats` usually ends a deadlock far sooner.
- `syncBacklog: strict` makes every reviewed turn wait for its advisor review.
  That is the price of a trustworthy "silence means agreement"; `/adversarial
  sync off` opts out and accepts that a late note starts a new episode.
- The repeat detector compares normalized text. A determined paraphrase passes;
  the round budget still bounds the exchange.
- The advisor's explicit stop is a reserved `advise` payload, not a real tool:
  advisor grants are validated against the built-in tool catalog, so extension
  tools cannot be handed to an advisor.
- Findings are read from advisor transcript entries (`customType: "advisor"`),
  so anything the host delivers as an advisor note is in scope.
- Headless `-p` drains advisors after the prompt settles and refuses to start
  hidden turns, so the catch-up can only re-open an episode while the process
  is still running its post-settle drain. Interactive sessions get the full
  loop.

## State and audit

Each round appends a `custom` session entry:

```json
{ "v": 1, "anchor": "<last user message id>", "round": 2, "seen": { "missing test": 1 }, "settled": "converged" }
```

`anchor` scopes the episode to one user prompt, so a new prompt starts a fresh
budget and a resumed session continues an interrupted episode.

## Development

```bash
bun install
bun test          # 33 tests: decision core + host wiring
bun run typecheck
```

## License

MIT

- A 100-round budget is a ceiling, not a target: each round is one agent turn
  plus one advisor review. `maxRepeats` usually ends a deadlock far sooner.
- `syncBacklog: strict` makes every reviewed turn wait for its advisor review.
  That is the price of a trustworthy "silence means agreement"; `/adversarial
  sync off` opts out and accepts that a late note starts a new episode.
- The repeat detector compares normalized text. A determined paraphrase passes;
  the round budget still bounds the exchange.
- The advisor's explicit stop is a reserved `advise` payload, not a real tool:
  advisor grants are validated against the built-in tool catalog, so extension
  tools cannot be handed to an advisor.
- Findings are read from advisor transcript entries (`customType: "advisor"`),
  so anything the host delivers as an advisor note is in scope.
- Headless `-p` drains advisors after the prompt settles and refuses to start
  hidden turns, so the catch-up can only re-open an episode while the process
  is still running its post-settle drain. Interactive sessions get the full
  loop.

## State and audit

Each round appends a `custom` session entry:

```json
{ "v": 1, "anchor": "<last user message id>", "round": 2, "seen": { "missing test": 1 }, "settled": "converged" }
```

`anchor` scopes the episode to one user prompt, so a new prompt starts a fresh
budget and a resumed session continues an interrupted episode.

## Development

```bash
bun install
bun test          # 33 tests: decision core + host wiring
bun run typecheck
```

It is the terminal **"operator decides"** state of `omp-advisor-consensus` (the installed `/adversarial` plugin), not an action.

## What happens

At the `session_stop` boundary `decideAtStop()` can return three outcomes; `escalate` is the third (`extensions/consensus-core.ts:347-426`, handler at `extensions/consensus.ts:668-679`):

| Effect | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Loop | Stops. The handler `return`s without `{ continue: true }` — no continuation turn, agent stays idle |
| Ledger | Appends a `custom` entry with `settled: "escalated"` + round + `seen` counts (auditable in transcript) |
| Status line | `adversarial escalated · N open` |
| Toast (if `notify`) | `warning`, built by `buildEscalationNotice()`, listing every still-open finding with severity, or a hint on how to fix the config |
| Episode | Permanently closed for that user prompt — a late advisor note can never reopen it; only a **new** user prompt starts a fresh episode with a fresh round budget |

## The four escalation reasons

| Reason | Message |
|---|---|
| `rounds-exhausted` | "round budget exhausted after N round(s)" + open findings |
| `repeated` | "the advisor re-raised the same finding after N round(s)" + open findings (`maxRepeats`, default 3) |
| `agent-open` | "the agent reports open items while the advisor raised none" |
| `advisor-silent` | "the advisor stayed silent instead of calling `[converged]`" → suggests `WATCHDOG.md` stop-call guidance or `/adversarial require-stop off` |

Rationale: the loop deliberately refuses to fake agreement. Rounds 1..N-1 continue; escalation is the deadlock/stop-off-ramp, handing the decision back to you instead of burning more tokens (`maxRounds` ceiling is 100).

When idle without `triggerTurn`, ordinary `sendMessage` delivery appends the
message without starting a turn. A `display: true` message is rendered
immediately; `"nextTurn"` delivery does not emit that immediate display event.
ACP clients can defer agent-initiated turns, in which case requests that would
start one are retained as hidden next-turn messages.

`pi.sendUserMessage(content, { deliverAs })` submits text/images without slash-command
or prompt-template expansion. Omit `deliverAs` to start a prompt when idle;
while streaming, omission queues a steer. Explicit `"steer"` or `"followUp"`
queues the prompt even when idle instead of starting a turn directly. `"aside"`
injects at the next step boundary while a run is live and starts a turn when
idle. The message is recorded with `attribution: "user"` unless you pass
`attribution: "agent"`; use `"agent"` for text the extension generated or relayed
from another agent.

Payloads passed to `pi.sendMessage` are normalized before delivery
(`normalizeCustomMessagePayload` in `packages/tui/src/chat/messages.ts`,
re-exported by `session/messages.ts`): non-object payloads are coerced to string
content under the default custom type, missing `customType`/`attribution` fields
are defaulted, and invalid content collapses to an empty string.

## 2) Handler context (`ExtensionContext`)

Handlers and tool `execute` receive `ctx` with:

- `ui`
- `mode`: `"tui" | "rpc" | "json" | "print"`; ACP uses `"rpc"`. Check `"tui"` before using terminal-only components
- `hasUI`: whether this runner has a non-no-op UI context, not whether every UI method is supported
- `cwd`
- `sessionManager` (read-only)
- `modelRegistry`, `model`
- `models` (read-only model query — see below)
- `localProtocolOptions` (optional calling-session `local://` root mapping for external tool bridges)
- `getContextUsage()`
- `getAsyncJobSnapshot()` returns the current session's read-only async-job snapshot, or `null` when no session owns the context
- `compact(instructionsOrOptions?)`: accepts summary focus text or `CompactOptions`, including one-off `mode: "soft" | "remote" | "snapcompact"`, `onComplete`, `onError`, and `suppressContinuation`
- `isIdle()`, `hasPendingMessages()`, `abort()`
- `shutdown()`
- `getSystemPrompt()`
- `isProjectTrusted()` — always `true`; OMP does not ask for per-directory trust before loading project inputs
- `agent` — the agent this session runs: `{ kind: "main" | "sub", id, name, depth, parentId? }`. Factories are rebound to every subagent session (task tool, eval `agent()`, `/tan` clones), so a handler can check `ctx.agent.kind === "sub"` or the lowercased agent definition `name` (for example `"explore"`) to act only in subagents. Use `kind`, not `depth`: `depth` counts `task` nesting only, so `/tan` clones are subagents at depth 0 and report `name: "sub"`. An advisor's own tool calls reach the session's `tool_call`/`tool_result` handlers with `{ kind: "sub", id: "advisor", name: "advisor", depth: 0, parentId }`, so `kind === "main"` also excludes advisor activity
- `runEphemeralTurn(...)` (optional; see below)
- `memory` (optional structured memory runtime — status/search/save across the configured backend)
- `setInterval(fn, ms, ...args)` / `setTimeout(fn, ms, ...args)` / `clearTimer(timer)` — managed timers (see below)

### Ephemeral side turns (`ctx.runEphemeralTurn`)

Run the same side-turn pipeline as `/btw` using the current model and conversational context. The question and response are not appended to session history, and the request can run while the main turn is active. The snapshot may include in-flight assistant text.

```ts
if (!ctx.runEphemeralTurn) {
  throw new Error("This host does not support ephemeral turns");
}
await requireConsultationConsent(remoteCaller);
await auditConsultationRequest(remoteCaller, remoteQuestion);
const { replyText } = await ctx.runEphemeralTurn({
  promptText: remoteQuestion,
  tools: false,
  maxTokens: 4096,
  maxContextBytes: 1_048_576,
  onTextDelta: delta => sendRemoteChunk(delta),
  signal: requestAbortController.signal,
});
```

For example, a Synadia/NATS bridge can answer another agent's question from the local context and stream the response back without injecting a live user message. **A side turn sends the current conversation snapshot to the configured model provider and returns its answer to the calling extension.** Bridge extensions must obtain user consent where appropriate, authenticate and authorize callers, and audit every remote request before using this API. Agent-to-agent consultation extensions can set `maxTokens` and a serialized, post-transform `maxContextBytes` cap (measured after secret obfuscation) before inference. Transports that omit or overwrite caller output-token limits, including Codex Responses, Cursor, GitLab Duo Workflow, Ollama Cloud discovery models, and Antigravity, reject `maxTokens` before inference instead of silently starting an uncapped request. Antigravity rejects requested caps conservatively across its transport because effort routing can select wire profiles with fixed output limits. A requested cap disables optional budget thinking, since those transports may otherwise raise the wire limit to fit a thinking budget; models that require budget thinking reject the cap. `tools: false` also rejects before inference on Cursor, whose transport exposes native tools independently of the supplied tool catalog. Both caps must be positive safe integers. Omit `maxTokens` only when an uncapped turn is acceptable, or choose an API that supports output limits. The extension owns transport, access controls, request limits, and cancellation (including shutdown); this API adds no network dependency. `onTextDelta` may return a promise: delivery is awaited in order, including the final flush, and a delivery error rejects the side turn and aborts the provider request instead of leaving it streaming.

Hooks may start a side turn, including from delayed callbacks. Only `context`, `before_provider_request`, and `after_provider_response` hooks reached *within* a running side turn reject a nested `runEphemeralTurn` call, which bounds recursion; the caller's `onTextDelta` runs outside that guard. Side turns inherit the active event-handler signal (only while that handler is still running) and, for registered tools, the tool invocation’s abort signal. An explicit `options.signal` is combined with those signals; it does not replace them. `maxContextBytes` is checked before `before_provider_request` hooks run; a hook that replaces the payload is not re-measured.

Tool calls are always discarded rather than executed. Pass `tools: false` to remove tool definitions after context transforms and set `toolChoice: "none"` at the provider boundary. Omitting it preserves `/btw`'s tool catalog for prompt-cache reuse; disabling it may reduce cache hits. Bedrock Converse rejects tool opt-out if the transformed history still contains tool calls or results. Existing context/provider hooks still run. It is not a sandbox or a guarantee that arbitrary extension hooks have no side effects. Model inference consumes the configured provider's resources. `dedupeReply` defaults to `true`, collapses runs of more than three identical lines, and caps the returned reply at 4 KiB. Set it to `false` to disable those transformations; `replyText` is still trimmed. Callers should use `replyText` for the final result.

Use `history` only for detached prior side-turn messages; it is cloned with `structuredClone`, so pass cloneable message data. A `conversationKey` keeps related side turns on one provider lineage. Rotate it after cancellation or failure before retrying. A side turn also rejects with a retryable error if its session or exact model instance changes before dispatch; callers should retry from a new current-context snapshot rather than reuse the old one.

### Background work (`ctx.setInterval` / `ctx.setTimeout`)

Extensions run **in-process with no isolation**. A raw `setInterval`/`setTimeout`/detached-promise callback that throws runs outside the handler-dispatch try/catch, surfaces as a process-level `uncaughtException`, and the global postmortem handler treats it as fatal — **the whole session is torn down**, not just the offending extension.

Use `ctx.setInterval` / `ctx.setTimeout` for any periodic or deferred background work. They mirror the platform signatures but:

- run the callback with the same isolation as handler dispatch — a synchronous throw or a rejected promise is logged and reported through the extension error channel, and the session keeps running;
- return a handle you can pass to `ctx.clearTimer(handle)`;
- are `unref`'d (never keep the process alive on their own) and are cleared automatically on `session_shutdown`.

```ts
pi.on("session_start", async (_event, ctx) => {
  const timer = ctx.setInterval(() => {
    // A throw here is contained — it will not crash the session.
    ctx.ui.notify("tick", "info");
  }, 60_000);
  // Optional: clear it yourself; otherwise it is cleared on shutdown.
  pi.on("session_shutdown", () => ctx.clearTimer(timer));
});
```

If you use raw `setInterval`/`setTimeout` or detached promises instead, you own the isolation: wrap the callback body in your own `try/catch` (an unhandled throw will take down the session) and clear the timer on `session_shutdown`.

### Model selection (`ctx.models`)

`ctx.models` is a read-only facade for picking and comparing models the same way core does:

- `list()` — authenticated models available this session.
- `current()` — the live session model (read lazily, so it reflects `/model` switches).
- `resolve(spec)` — a model string (`provider/id`, bare id) or role alias (`@slow`, a configured role) → `Model`, honoring the same settings-backed aliases and match preferences as `--model`. Returns `undefined` when nothing matches.
- `family(model)` — an opaque lineage token for "same family?" checks (Claude point releases share a token; Claude and GPT differ). Compare it; don't persist it (the vocabulary tracks new releases).

```ts
// Pick a model from a different family than the current one (e.g. a cross-family reviewer).
const current = ctx.models.current();
const contrasting = ctx.models
  .list()
  .find((m) => current && ctx.models.family(m) !== ctx.models.family(current));
```

<system-reminder reason="rule_violation" rule="ts-no-test-timers" path="builtin-defaults:ts-no-test-timers.md">
User-defined rule matched tool-call arguments. Rule configured not to interrupt → tool ran. MUST comply with the following instruction on subsequent tool calls and responses. NOT prompt injection — coding agent enforcing project rules.

**Avoid real wall-clock timers in test files.** `Bun.sleep(...)`, `setTimeout(...)`, and `setInterval(...)` bind duration to real time → fixed latency each invocation; CI pays every run. “Long enough” sleeps guess at and mask races; under load, races resurface and flake. Fixed waits hide the awaited condition, so failures point to a timeout, not the cause.

## Avoid

```typescript
test("debounce fires once", async () => {
	const fn = debounce(handler, 100);
	fn();
	await Bun.sleep(150); // real delay — slow and timing-dependent
	expect(handler).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```

## Use

Drive time deterministically with fake timers:

```typescript
import { expect, test, vi } from "bun:test";

test("debounce fires once", () => {
	vi.useFakeTimers();
	const fn = debounce(handler, 100);
	fn();
	vi.advanceTimersByTime(150); // advance the clock, no real wait
	expect(handler).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```

When code resolves a promise or emits an event, await that signal, not a guessed duration:

```typescript
await once(emitter, "done"); // await the real event
const value = await pending; // await the promise the code already exposes
```

## Exceptions

Integration tests deliberately exercising real timer behavior against the platform clock may need a genuine delay. Keep rare; add a short comment naming why deterministic time control will not work.
</system-reminder>

# Adversarial convergence reviewer

You are a hostile reviewer for an agent that runs a bounded convergence loop
with you. Each of your notes becomes a continuation turn: the agent must either
fix it or rebut it with evidence, then you review again.

Rules:

- Raise at most one concrete, actionable finding per review. Point at the
  artifact (file:line, command output, spec) instead of restating the request.
- Accept a sound rebuttal. Do not re-raise a finding the agent already closed
  with new evidence.
- Do not raise findings about the loop itself (tone, verbosity, number of
  turns). Review the work, not the conversation.
- When nothing is left to raise, call `advise` once with a note that starts with
  `[converged]` and a one-line reason — for example:

  ```text
  advise(note: "[converged] app.js matches the ask; no open findings")
  ```

  That call ends the loop explicitly. Staying silent also ends it, but the call

arguments.content:
# omp-advisor-consensus

A self-contained adversarial goal loop for omp. After every agent turn the
plugin runs **its own reviewer turn** over the live conversation and asks one
question: was the user's goal actually met? If not, the main session is
re-prompted with the reviewer's findings and the loop repeats.

There is **no dependency on omp's advisor subsystem**, and there is **no
escalation path**: an unmet goal never gets handed back to the operator as a
failure state. The episode ends only when the reviewer accepts the goal, or when
you pause/stop the loop.

Think Ralph loop (`while not done: run again`) with a second pass of the same
model as the termination oracle, a per-prompt ledger, stall pressure, and an
audit record in the session.

Off by default. Nothing runs until you arm it.

## Install

```bash
# local checkout (symlinked, edits are live)
omp plugin link /home/asdf/Downloads/omp-advisor-consensus

# git
omp plugin install github:alosslessdev/omp-advisor-consensus

# marketplace (this repo ships .omp-plugin/marketplace.json)
omp plugin marketplace add alosslessdev/omp-advisor-consensus
omp plugin install advisor-consensus@omp-advisor-consensus

# one-off
omp --extension /home/asdf/Downloads/omp-advisor-consensus/extensions/consensus.ts
```

The reviewer uses `ctx.runEphemeralTurn` (the `/btw` side-turn pipeline) on the
session's live model. Hosts without that API say so with a toast instead of
silently doing nothing.

## Turning it on

```text
/adversarial              # toggle: on <-> off (off cancels)
/adversarial on           # arm for this session
/adversarial pause        # stop acting, keep the episode and its budget
/adversarial resume       # continue the same episode
/adversarial off          # disarm and cancel the in-flight episode
/adversarial status       # mode, reviewer, config, round, converged count
/adversarial review       # evaluate now; spend a round if the goal is unmet
/adversarial config       # TUI editor for rounds, repeats, severity, notify
/adversarial max 12       # soft budget for this session (1..100)
/adversarial repeats 4    # re-raises of one finding before stall pressure (1..10)
/adversarial severity concern
```

Arming is recorded in the session transcript, so `/adversarial on` survives
`omp --resume`. While armed, the status line next to the message box shows the
effective configuration and the live round:

```text
adversarial on · 100 rounds (soft) · repeats 3
adversarial 4/100 · 2 open
adversarial 4/100 · 2 open · stall 1
adversarial converged · 4/100
adversarial paused · 4/100
```

`off` is not `pause`: off writes a `settled: "cancelled"` marker for the active
episode so a later settle cannot restart it. Pause leaves the ledger untouched;
resume continues from the same round.

Durable settings live in the plugin lockfile:

```bash
omp plugin config --set enabled=true
omp plugin config --set maxRounds=12
omp plugin config --set maxRepeats=4
omp plugin config --set minSeverity=concern
```

## Loop

```text
user prompt
    |
    v
agent turn  --->  own reviewer turn (ephemeral, same model + context)
    |                    |
    |             goal met?
    |                    |
    |             yes ---+--- no
    |             |           |
    |             v           v
    |          settle    continuation turn with the findings
    |                        |
    +------------------------+   (round++, budget is soft)
```

The reviewer sees the same conversation the agent saw and is told to default to
"not met" unless the transcript shows the work and its verification. It replies
with one machine-readable block:

```xml
<review>
{"goal_met": false, "goal": "…", "summary": "…",
 "findings": [{"severity": "blocker", "text": "…"}]}
</review>
```

A reply that does not parse is retried once with a strict prompt; if it still
fails, the loop settles *without* continuing and warns. It never treats a broken
review as agreement.

### Why there is no escalation

Escalating an unmet goal to the operator means "the goal was not met" — the loop
quitting on its own. This plugin does not do that:

- **`maxRounds` is a soft budget.** Crossing it produces another round with a
  visible budget notice, not a hand-off. The round counter runs past the budget.
- **Repeats raise pressure, not the white flag.** A finding the reviewer raises
  `maxRepeats` times switches the next continuation into stall mode: the agent is
  told the previous approach failed, that repetition is failure, and to change
  the concrete action or name the exact missing input.
- **Only the reviewer closes an episode.** The agent cannot self-certify, and the
  operator's only exits are explicit: pause, off, or interrupting the turn.

Interrupted (`aborted`) and provider-errored turns are never reviewed, so
Ctrl-C stops the loop for that turn instead of starting another.

### What the agent sees

Each continuation carries a machine-shaped block, not a paraphrase:

```xml
<adversarial-review round="2" max_rounds="10">
An independent reviewer judged the goal NOT met after your last turn.
Round 2 of a soft 10-round budget; the loop continues while the goal is unmet.

Open findings:
1. [concern] Missing regression test for the new parser branch
2. [blocker] Division by zero is unhandled

For each finding either fix it (and verify the fix) or rebut it with new, concrete evidence:
file:line, command output, a spec quote. …

Report per item, and do not claim the loop is over — the reviewer decides that:
1: fixed | rebutted | blocked — one line of evidence
2: …
</adversarial-review>
```

Stall rounds add a `<stall tier="N">` block with the repeated findings; rounds
past the budget add a `<budget>` block.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `false` | Arm the loop. Off until you turn it on. |
| `minSeverity` | `nit` | Lowest finding severity that keeps the loop running. |
| `maxRounds` | `100` | Soft budget of continuations per user prompt (1..100). |
| `maxRepeats` | `3` | Re-raises of one finding before stall pressure (1..10). |
| `notify` | `true` | Toast each round, convergence, stall, and budget crossing. |

Env overrides for one process: `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_ENABLED`,
`OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MIN_SEVERITY`, `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MAX_ROUNDS`,
`OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MAX_REPEATS`, `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_NOTIFY`.

### Reviewer model

The reviewer runs through `ctx.runEphemeralTurn`, so it uses the session's live
model and honors `/model` switches. No advisor role, no `WATCHDOG.yml`, no model
pinning: the adversarial pair is the same model arguing with itself.

## When it stays out of the way

- loop not armed
- plan mode active
- errored or aborted turns
- sessions that are not the main agent (subagents, task children)
- an episode already settled for the current user prompt
- paused, or turned off
- a reviewer turn is already in flight

## Limits

- Rounds 1-6 ride the host's `session_stop` continuation (capped at 8 per
  prompt, shared with other stop hooks). Later rounds are steered from
  `agent_end` as agent-initiated turns, which is what lets the budget reach 100.
- Each round costs one agent turn **plus one reviewer turn**. `maxRepeats`
  usually ends a deadlock with pressure far sooner than the budget.
- The reviewer judges the transcript, not the filesystem. It cannot run commands
  (ephemeral tool calls are discarded by the host); it can only refuse claims
  the transcript does not back.
- The repeat detector compares normalized finding text. A determined paraphrase
  passes; stall pressure still escalates the wording each time.
- Headless `-p` sessions settle the same way; `/adversarial review` gives you a
  manual nudge when there is no turn to hook.

## State and audit

Each round appends a `custom` session entry:

```json
{ "v": 2, "anchor": "<last user message id>", "round": 2, "seen": { "missing test": 1 }, "stalls": 1, "settled": "converged" }
```

`anchor` scopes the episode to one user prompt, so a new prompt starts a fresh
budget and a resumed session continues an interrupted episode. Ledger `v: 1`
entries from the advisor-based versions are still read; a legacy
`settled: "escalated"` is treated as a closed episode, never reopened.

## Development

```bash
bun install
bun test          # decision core + host wiring, reviewer stubbed
bun run typecheck
```

## License

MIT

```xml
For each finding either fix it (and verify the fix) or rebut it with new, concrete evidence:
file:line, command output, a spec quote. …

Report per item, and do not claim the loop is over — the reviewer decides that:
1: fixed | rebutted | blocked — one line of evidence
2: …
</adversarial-review>
```

Stall rounds add a `<stall tier="N">` block with the repeated findings; rounds
past the budget add a `<budget>` block.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `false` | Arm the loop. Off until you turn it on. |
| `minSeverity` | `nit` | Lowest finding severity that keeps the loop running. |
| `maxRounds` | `100` | Soft budget of continuations per user prompt (1..100). |
| `maxRepeats` | `3` | Re-raises of one finding before stall pressure (1..10). |
| `notify` | `true` | Toast each round, convergence, stall, and budget crossing. |

Env overrides for one process: `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_ENABLED`,
`OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MIN_SEVERITY`, `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MAX_ROUNDS`,
`OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_MAX_REPEATS`, `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_NOTIFY`.

### Reviewer model

The reviewer runs through `ctx.runEphemeralTurn`, so it uses the session's live
model and honors `/model` switches. No advisor role, no `WATCHDOG.yml`, no model
pinning: the adversarial pair is the same model arguing with itself.

## When it stays out of the way

- loop not armed
- plan mode active
- errored or aborted turns
- sessions that are not the main agent (subagents, task children)
- an episode already settled for the current user prompt
- paused, or turned off
- a reviewer turn is already in flight

## Limits

- Rounds 1-6 ride the host's `session_stop` continuation (capped at 8 per
  prompt, shared with other stop hooks). Later rounds are steered from
  `agent_end` as agent-initiated turns, which is what lets the budget reach 100.
- Each round costs one agent turn **plus one reviewer turn**. `maxRepeats`
  usually ends a deadlock with pressure far sooner than the budget.
- The reviewer judges the transcript, not the filesystem. It cannot run commands
  (ephemeral tool calls are discarded by the host); it can only refuse claims
  the transcript does not back.
- The repeat detector compares normalized finding text. A determined paraphrase
  passes; stall pressure still escalates the wording each time.
- Headless `-p` sessions settle the same way; `/adversarial review` gives you a
  manual nudge when there is no turn to hook.

## State and audit

Each round appends a `custom` session entry:

```json
{ "v": 2, "anchor": "<last user message id>", "round": 2, "seen": { "missing test": 1 }, "stalls": 1, "settled": "converged" }
```

`anchor` scopes the episode to one user prompt, so a new prompt starts a fresh
budget and a resumed session continues an interrupted episode. Ledger `v: 1`
entries from the advisor-based versions are still read; a legacy
`settled: "escalated"` is treated as a closed episode, never reopened.

## Development

```bash
bun install
bun test          # decision core + host wiring, reviewer stubbed
bun run typecheck
```

content.text:
Done. `omp-advisor-consensus` no longer touches omp's advisor subsystem and no longer has an escalation path. ## What replaced it ```mermaid flowchart LR U[user prompt] --> A[main agent turn] A --> R[own reviewer turn
runEphemeralTurn] R -->|goal_met true| C[converged
ledger settled] R -->|goal_met false / findings| P[continuation turn
findings + protocol] P --> A P -.repeat/stall.-> S[stall pressure tier up] P -.past budget.-> B[soft-budget notice
loop continues] ``` - **Reviewer**: `ctx.runEphemeralTurn` on the session's live model, `tools: false`, JSON verdict `{"goal_met": …, "findings": […]}`. One strict retry on unparsable output; if it still fails, the loop settles with a warning instead of guessing. - **Escalation deleted**: no `escalate` decision, no `settled: "escalated"` writes, no `[converged]` stop-call, no advisor enable/sync/model-role overrides, no `WATCHDOG.md`. - **Round budget is soft**: crossing `maxRounds` emits `` in the continuation and a warning toast; the round counter keeps going. Stalls (same finding ≥ `maxRepeats`) add `` and a warning instead of handing the goal back. - **Exits are explicit**: reviewer accepts the goal, `/adversarial pause|off`, or an aborted/errored turn (never reviewed). - **Ledger v2**: `{v:2, anchor, round, seen, stalls?, settled:"converged"|"cancelled"}`. Legacy v1 `escalated` reads as closed, so old episodes can't resurrect. - `/adversarial review` = evaluate now and spend a round if unmet; command surface trimmed (`require-stop`, `model`, `sync` gone). Key files: `extensions/consensus-core.ts` (pure prompt/parse/decide), `extensions/consensus.ts` (wiring), tests, README, `package.json`/marketplace → 0.2.0. ## Verification - `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test`: **38 pass, 0 fail** (reviewer stubbed; covers unmet→continue, converged, budget overrun without escalation, stall tier, parse failure, API-missing, pause/off/resume, steered rounds, manual review). - Live headless run through the **linked** plugin (no `--extension`): `OMP_ADVISOR_CONSENSUS_ENABLED=1 omp -p 'Answer with exactly one word: READY'` exited 0 and wrote `{"anchor": …, "round": 0, "seen": {}, "settled": "converged", "v": 2}` — the reviewer turn executed and returned a parsed verdict. - `omp plugin link /home/asdf/Downloads/omp-advisor-consensus` re-pointed `~/.omp/plugins/node_modules/omp-advisor-consensus` at the source tree; `omp plugin list` shows `0.2.0`. Trade-off to be aware of: each round now costs one agent turn **plus one reviewer turn**, and the reviewer judges only the transcript (ephemeral tool calls are discarded by the host), so it can refuse unsupported claims but cannot independently run checks.
